name: ABBMUN (Abbotsleigh Model United Nations Conference)
description: School-hosted one-day Model United Nations conference run annually by Abbotsleigh Senior School in Wahroonga. A low-cost introductory MUN experience building diplomacy, negotiation and public speaking skills.
registration_window: Usually closes mid-March

name: Abstract Art Competition
description: International online abstract art competition open to artists worldwide, hosted by Contemporary Art Room Gallery.
registration_window: Entries usually due early June

name: AFS Global You Changemaker
organiser: AFS Intercultural Programs (with the University of Pennsylvania)
cost: Tuition applies; advanced content around USD 245
description: A 12 week online certificate program designed by AFS and the University of Pennsylvania. Teens explore global citizenship, social impact and design thinking and develop their own social impact project, finishing with an Advanced Certificate on Global Citizenship for Social Impact. Requires advanced written and spoken English.
registration_window: Monthly cohorts run year round; choose preferred dates after registering

name: ALHR School Student Forum on Human Rights
location: Varies (2023: Newcastle; 2025: NSW Parliament House, Sydney)
description: Annual one-day human rights forum run by ALHR with the University of Newcastle and the Human Rights for NSW Alliance. Around 60 NSW students explore a human rights theme with legal professionals and advocates, producing a formal statement presented to decision-makers.
registration_window: Schools nominate students ahead of the September forum

name: AMOC Senior Contest
description: Invitational senior maths contest run by the Australian Mathematical Olympiad Committee under the AMT. Around 100 students (mostly Year 11) sit five problems over four hours covering geometry, number theory, algebra and combinatorics. A key step on the pathway to APMO, EGMO and IMO teams.
registration_window: By invitation, based on prior AMT results

name: ANSTO Think Science
organiser: Australian Nuclear Science and Technology Organisation (ANSTO)
description: Nationwide science competition run by ANSTO. Students work in teams to design and conduct a scientific investigation, then submit their findings in video form.
registration_window: Registrations usually open around February

name: Anthology Short Story Competition
description: Open international short story competition for original, previously unpublished stories in English, hosted by Anthology Magazine. Winning story is published in the magazine.
registration_window: Entries usually due early July

name: Anthology Travel Writing Competition
description: Open international travel writing competition for original, previously unpublished articles in English, hosted by Anthology Magazine. Winning piece is published in the magazine.
registration_window: Entries usually due end of November

name: ANU STEM Challenges
organiser: ANU College of Science and Medicine
description: Weekly hands-on STEM challenges run by ANU. A new challenge is released each Tuesday across science, technology, engineering and maths; students submit photos, answers or builds by Sunday, judged by ANU staff.
registration_window: Rolling weekly challenges; join any time during the season

name: APA TOPSS Competition
description: Annual video competition run by the American Psychological Association's Teachers of Psychology in Secondary Schools (TOPSS). Students create a short video applying psychological science to a set annual topic. Open to international high school students; up to five entries per school, no team submissions.
registration_window: Entries usually due around March

name: APSMO – Maths Explorer (Years 3 & 4)
cost: AUD 180 per team of up to 30 (early-bird AUD 160)
description: Collaborative problem-solving contest series for Years 3–4 from APSMO. Four contest papers per year sat at school, with Resource Kits, videos, activity sheets and worked solutions for teachers.
registration_window: Register before Term 2; papers run May to September

name: APSMO – Maths Games (Junior, Years 5 & 6)
cost: Per-team registration via APSMO (see website for current fees)
description: Four non-competitive contest papers aligned to the Maths Olympiad schedule, for mainstream and mixed-ability classes in Years 5–6. Resource Kits with sample questions and solutions precede each paper.
registration_window: Register before Term 2; papers run May to September

name: APSMO Maths Olympiad
cost: AUD 180 first team, then AUD 140 per additional team
description: Prestigious APSMO Maths Olympiad for high-potential Years 5–6 students. Running since 1987, it develops problem-solving through a series of five olympiad-style contest papers.
registration_window: Register before Term 2; contests run May to September

name: ASX Schools Sharemarket Game
location: Online (Australia and New Zealand). Sat at school or home.
description: Online sharemarket simulation run twice yearly by the ASX. Students manage a virtual portfolio, buying and selling shares in ASX-listed companies over a ten-week window, individually or in syndicates of 2–4. Cash prizes at state and national level.
registration_window: Two game windows per year (~10 weeks each)

name: ATYP Drama Ensembles
description: Weekly term ensembles covering script analysis, character development, voice, movement and devising, finishing with an Open Studio performance.
registration_window: Weekly term ensembles; early bird discounts

name: ATYP Holiday Workshops
description: Five day holiday workshops such as Bad to the Bard and Transform AHHHH, covering script analysis, character development and devising, finishing with a family performance showcase.
registration_window: School holiday workshops across the year

name: Australasian Philosothon (Online / Hybrid)
description: The Australasian final of the Philosothon movement, assessed by university philosophers. Teams of one student per year level (Years 8–12) take part in Communities of Inquiry, judged on philosophical inquiry, clarity and reasoning. Runs online or hybrid.
registration_window: Register ahead of the late-August event

name: Australian and New Zealand Brain Bee Challenge ABBC
location: Online (Round 1); university hosts for regional finals
organiser: Australian and New Zealand Brain Bee Challenge
description: Neuroscience competition for Year 10 students across three rounds. Round 1 sat online via Education Perfect; regional finals in person; national final online. National finalists may have travel and accommodation supported.
registration_link: Education Perfect event page or through EP school portal
registration_window: Register before the Round 1 window (around March)

name: Australian Economics and Business Studies Competition (AEBSC)
description: Annual paper-based competition for senior students assessing economic and business theory, run by a volunteer committee at the UNSW Business School. Around 15,000+ students from 900+ schools participate each year.
registration_window: Register before the annual assessment date

name: Australian Economics Olympiad (AEO)
organiser: Consortium for Inclusive Economics Education (CIEE), UNSW Sydney
description: National economics enrichment competition for high school students run by the Consortium for Inclusive Economics Education at UNSW Sydney. Tests mastery of economics, problem solving and economic reasoning. Top performers form the Australian team for the international olympiads.
registration_window: Register before the May sitting

name: Australian Geography Competition AGC
description: National multiple-choice geography competition sat at school. All participants receive certificates; top performers earn distinctions. High-performing senior students may be selected for Geography's Big Week Out and the International Geography Olympiad team.
registration_window: Usually late January – early May

name: Australian History Competition AHC
cost: AUD 50 school fee + AUD 8 per student
description: National multiple-choice history test for Years 7–10, with two papers (Years 7–8 and Years 9–10). State champions receive medallions and national champions receive leather portfolios.
registration_window: Registrations usually close around March

name: Australian Informatics Olympiad AIO
description: Three-hour programming contest run by the Australian Maths Trust in C, C++, Java or Python. The national entry point to the informatics olympiad pathway; high performers may be invited to AMT high-performance programs.
registration_window: Register via AMT before the late-August contest

name: Australian Intermediate Mathematics Olympiad (AIMO)
location: At school (school-supervised, paper printed by teacher; solutions submitted digitally)
description: Highly challenging four-hour olympiad-style mathematics paper run by the AMT, pitched at Year 10 level but suited to talented Years 7–9 students. Ten questions including written proofs; feeds the AMT olympiad pathway.
registration_window: Entries usually close early September; sat mid-September

name: Australian Mathematical Olympiad (AMO) — AMO Summer, AMO Winter and AMO Finals
location: AMO Summer and AMO Winter: at school (invitational). AMO Finals: AMT-organised exam hubs (invitational)
description: Australia's senior invitational maths olympiad pathway, structured as three competitions: AMO Summer (February, at school), AMO Winter and AMO Finals (AMT exam hubs). Around 200–250 students in Year 11 or below are invited, feeding the School of Excellence and IMO team selection.
registration_window: By invitation from AMOC State Directors

name: Australian Mathematics Competition AMC
description: Australia's flagship school mathematics competition, administered by the Australian Maths Trust since 1978. A 30-question challenge sat online or on paper across five divisions from Middle Primary to Senior.
registration_window: Register via AMT before the early-August sitting

name: Australian Mental Health Awareness Essay Competition (AMHAEC)
description: Australian essay competition on mental health awareness for students aged 13–18, with Junior (Years 7–8), Intermediate (Years 9–10) and Senior (Years 11–12) divisions. 800-word limit on an annual prompt.
registration_window: Entries usually due mid-August

name: Australian Science Olympiad Exams ASO
cost: AUD 16.50 per student per exam (Earth & Environmental Science free)
description: The selection exams for the Australian Science Olympiads pathway, run by ASI in Biology, Chemistry, Physics and Earth & Environmental Science. High performers may be invited to the residential ASO Summer School and on to International Science Olympiad teams.
registration_window: Register before the late July–August exam window

name: Australian Science Olympiads Summer School
description: Invitation-only residential summer school run by Australian Science Innovations as part of the Australian Science Olympiads pathway. Students attend in one discipline (Biology, Chemistry, Earth & Environmental Science or Physics) and may be selected for International Science Olympiad teams.
registration_window: By invitation following the ASO Exams (sat August)

name: Australian Space Design Competition ASDC
location: Australia-wide; finals at The University of Queensland
cost: Approx. AUD 250 per team (qualifying); finals fees additional
description: Teams (2–12 students) respond to an engineering Request For Tender over the school year. Qualifying proposals lead to a two-day national final at The University of Queensland, with the winning team representing Australia at the International Space Settlement Design Competition.
registration_window: Registrations run April to June; proposals due mid-year

name: Australian Video Game Challenge
description: Australian STEM Video Game Challenge in which students design and develop a video game, combining creativity with technical and computational skills.
registration_window: Register before the mid-year submission deadline

name: Author of Tomorrow Award
description: An adventure fiction writing award run by the Wilbur and Niso Smith Foundation in the United Kingdom.
registration_window: TBA

name: Bebras Computational Thinking Challenge
description: International computational thinking challenge coordinated in Australia by the Australian Maths Trust. Fifteen short logic problems with no coding required, sat online individually or in teams of up to four. Divisions cover Years 3–12.
registration_window: Register via AMT before the February–March challenge window

name: Best Australian Yarn
description: A national short story competition with significant prize money, including youth categories.
registration_window: TBA

name: Better Read Kids Competition
description: A young writers' competition run by the Better Read Kids program.
registration_window: TBA

name: Big Science Competition
cost: Approx. AUD 9 per student (confirm with ASI)
description: A 50-minute online, mixed-format science competition run by Australian Science Innovations for Years 7–10. Tests scientific knowledge, critical thinking and problem solving across biology, chemistry, Earth & environmental science and physics. Now offered globally.
registration_window: Register before the May testing window

name: BIOTech Futures Challenge
description: Eight-week mentored research program for student teams tackling real-world challenges in medicine and sustainability, working with expert mentors and presenting at a Symposium at the University of Sydney.
registration_window: Registrations usually open May, close mid-July

name: Black and White Photo Awards
description: International black and white photography competition across five categories: Architecture, Street, Wildlife, Portrait and Landscape. Open to high school students through to professionals.
registration_window: Entries usually due mid-June

name: Blockly.Comp
description: Programming competition using visual block-based coding, designed for school students and teachers to learn programming concepts in an accessible, beginner-friendly format.
registration_window: Register via Grok Academy before the event

name: Bond Uni National High School Mooting Competition
location: Bond University, Gold Coast QLD (and online rounds)
description: National high school mooting competition hosted by Bond University, in which students argue appellate-style legal problems before judges, developing legal reasoning and advocacy.
registration_window: Register before the competition rounds

name: Bond University Film & Television Awards (BUFTA)
location: Online entry; awards night at Bond University, Gold Coast QLD
description: Bond University's short-film competition for Year 11–12 students across Australia and internationally — 'Bond's answer to the Oscars'. Eight genre categories with films up to 10 minutes; the top prize is a full film and television scholarship.
registration_window: Entries usually close early October; awards in November

name: Bond University High School Model United Nations (BUHMUN) conference
description: High school Model United Nations conference hosted by Bond University, in which students debate global issues as UN delegates, developing diplomacy, negotiation and public speaking.
registration_window: Register before the conference

name: Bond University Research and Statistics in Psychology
description: Bond University program introducing senior students to research methods and statistics in psychology. Details are limited — confirm current offering, dates and cost with Bond University.
registration_window: Confirm dates with Bond University

name: Bond University Year 12 Extension Program
description: Free two-day curriculum enrichment workshop at Bond University (Gold Coast) for Year 12 students, in either a Business or Maths stream. Small-group access to academics and current students, with part-fee scholarships for top performers.
registration_window: Usually opens early in the year; runs around April

name: Brain Bee Bootcamp
description: Official 16-week online International Brain Bee and IYNA prep program working through the Brain Facts book — written exam prep, patient diagnosis, neuroanatomy and neurohistology — with expert mentorship and a final mock exam. About 3–4 hours per week.
registration_window: Rolling enrolment across the 16-week season (roughly December to March)

name: Brain Essay Competition (Oxford Academic)
description: Annual essay competition run by Brain, the international neurology journal published by Oxford Academic. Seeks enlightening, well-written essays for a general readership (not academic papers); winning essays are published in the journal's Essay section.
registration_window: Entries usually due around October

name: BRAINways Quest Tutorials (Sydney)
location: Sydney (university campus venue advised prior to the program)
cost: $99 per day; $196 for two days (2026 Sydney pricing)
description: Single day tutorial program run by BRAINways Education for high potential primary and early secondary students in Sydney. Students are nominated by their school, then parents enrol online. Topics for this round are The Mathematics of Games, The Chemistry in a Prescription: The Science of Pain, and What is Art? The Philosophy of Beauty.
registration_window: Enrolments opened 10 August 2026 and close 1 October 2026, or earlier once places fill

name: British Psychology Olympiad (BPO)
description: Three-round psychology olympiad organised by Minds Underground and officially recommended by the University of Oxford. Open internationally to Years 9–12. Australian students select their equivalent UK year group on registration.
registration_window: Register before the February first round

name: Busan International Textile Design Competition
description: International textile design competition open to high school students and older, with an open theme. Hosted by the Busan Textile & Fashion Industries Association, with a substantial prize pool.
registration_window: Entries usually due early October

name: Cambridge Re:Think Essay Competition (CCIR)
description: International essay competition run by the Cambridge Centre for International Research for students aged 11–18, split into Junior and Senior divisions. Essays of 1,000–2,000 words on prompts spanning humanities, sciences and social sciences. Award ceremony at King's College, Cambridge.
registration_window: Entries usually due around 10 May

name: CANSW Latin and Greek Reading Competition
location: Heats at member schools; Finals at host venue in Sydney
description: Annual Latin and Greek reading competition for Years 10–11 run by the Classical Association of NSW. Students perform classical texts aloud, judged on pronunciation and expression. The Year 10 Chorus trophy honours Professor Kevin Lee.
registration_window: Heats June–July; state finals August

name: Carol Manners Essay Competition
organiser: Classical Languages Teachers Association (CLTA) of NSW
description: Annual Latin essay competition for Year 12 students run by the CLTA of NSW, established in 1998 in honour of classics teacher Carol Manners. Students respond to essay questions on their prescribed HSC and IB Latin texts; winning essays are published in the journal Classicum.
registration_window: Submissions due around July

name: CaseCatalyst Virtual Case Competition
description: Global virtual business case competition for high school students run by CaseCatalyst. Teams of 3–4 solve real-world challenges faced by early-stage startups in developing and emerging economies, finishing with a live Pitch Day before founders and judges.
registration_window: Entries usually close around April

name: City Lights Art Challenge
description: International art and photography competition themed around city lights at night — neon, streetlights, high-rise windows and motion in the dark. Hosted by Ten Moir Gallery; open to artists and photographers worldwide.
registration_window: Entries usually due late May

name: CLTA Latin Reading Competition (Year 9)
location: Host school in Sydney (recent years: Cranbrook School)
organiser: Classical Languages Teachers Association (CLTA) of NSW
description: Annual Latin reading competition for Year 9 students run by the CLTA of NSW. Students prepare and perform Latin passages aloud, judged on pronunciation, expression, phrasing and understanding. Complements the CANSW competition for Years 10–11.
registration_window: Register through CLTA ahead of the August event

name: CLTA Year 8 Latin Camp (Classics Camp)
organiser: Classical Languages Teachers Association (CLTA) of NSW
cost: Camp fee covers accommodation, meals and activities (via CLTA)
description: Residential Latin and classics camp for Year 8 students run by the CLTA of NSW. Brings together Latin students from many NSW schools for several days of immersive classics activities, language work and social events.
registration_window: Usually Term 3–4; dates circulated to CLTA member schools

name: Coding Challenge
description: Online coding competition for school students across multiple levels, run by Grok Academy.
registration_window: Register via Grok Academy before the event

name: Color Open Call 2026 — Grid Photo Gallery
description: International open call for photographers submitting works where colour plays a central role, hosted by Grid Photo Gallery.
registration_window: Entries usually due mid-June

name: Computational and Algorithmic Thinking CAT
description: National and international problem-solving competition run by the Australian Maths Trust focusing on computational and algorithmic thinking. No coding required.
registration_window: Register via AMT before the March competition window

name: Conrad Challenge
description: Global innovation competition for students aged 13–18 working in teams of 2–5 to solve real-world problems across categories such as Aerospace & Aviation, Cyber-Technology & Security, Energy & Environment and Health & Nutrition.
registration_window: Register before the entry rounds (usually from August)

name: Cordless Lamp Innovation Contest
description: Open design challenge to create a cordless lamp for off-grid contexts, hosted by Desall with a leading lighting company. Open to everyone worldwide.
registration_window: Entries usually due late June

name: Craig Silvey Award for Young Writers
description: An original prose competition of up to 2000 words, open to Western Australian school students in Years 1 to 12.
registration_window: Closes mid August
not_available_reason: Open to Western Australian school students only

name: Cyber Comp
description: Online competition testing students' cyber security skills and knowledge of digital safety, run by Grok Academy.
registration_window: Register via Grok Academy before the event

name: da Vinci Decathlon
location: Regional host schools; national finals at Knox Grammar
cost: Set by each host school; nationals fee published separately
description: Academic gala for teams of eight competing across ten disciplines (engineering, mathematics and chess, code breaking, art and poetry, science, English, ideation, creative producers, cartography and legacy). Regional rounds lead to national finals at Knox Grammar.
registration_window: Regionals in Term 2; register via host school beforehand

name: DMUN African Union and Arab League
description: Online conference on the DMUN Discover MUN series simulating regional multilateral bodies: the African Union's Peace and Security Council and Commission, and the Council of the Arab League. Beginner-level committees on African and Middle Eastern crises.
registration_window: Registrations close shortly before the late-September event

name: DMUN AMHS
description: Online Model UN on the DMUN circuit themed Action, Mystery, History and Story. Delegates serve on war-council and crisis committees set across historical, present-day and speculative future scenarios. Free and open worldwide.
registration_window: Registrations close shortly before the late-July event

name: DMUN Championship
description: Flagship year-end online conference of the DMUN circuit (around 500 delegates). Committees span Asian Parliamentary Debate, UNFCCC, ICJ, UNEP, Lok Sabha, European Parliament, a Historical Crisis Committee and the Council of the Arab League.
registration_window: Registrations close shortly before the early-December event

name: DMUN Conventions
description: Online conference on the DMUN circuit simulating the Conferences of the Parties (COPs) to three major UN environmental treaties: UNFCCC (climate), CBD (biodiversity) and UNCCD (desertification). Three beginner-level committees; around 500 delegates.
registration_window: Registrations close shortly before the September event

name: DMUN CRISIS
description: Online crisis-format MUN on the DMUN circuit with fast-moving committees spanning historical, fictional and contemporary scenarios — from a Historical Crisis Committee and UNSC to zombie-apocalypse and AI-governance crises.
registration_window: Registrations close shortly before the late-October event

name: DMUN Debate Forum
description: Online debate competition run by the DMUN Foundation in Asian Parliamentary and British Parliamentary formats. A large global event (around 2,000 delegates) with cash prizes for top performers.
registration_window: Registrations close shortly before the late-January event

name: DMUN INNOVA 2026: The DMUN Foundation Innovation Forum
description: Online innovation forum run by the DMUN Foundation, held 11 to 12 July 2026 with around 500 delegates from university and school students. Delegates explore creative problem solving, diplomacy and global cooperation, designing solutions for challenges in technology, governance, economics and society. Theme: Innovating for Inclusive and Sustainable Development. Enquiries: enquiries@dmun.org
registration_window: Chairs: 1 Apr to 5 Jul 2026. Delegates: 5 Apr to 12 Jul 2026. Observers: 14 Aug 2025 to 11 Jul 2026.

name: DMUN MEU: DMUN Model European Union
description: Online Model European Union simulation run by the DMUN Foundation. A two-day conference across three chambers (European Parliament, European Commission, European Central Bank) focused on consensus building and negotiation among the 27 member states.
registration_window: Registrations close shortly before the June event

name: DMUN Moot Court
description: Online legal simulation conference on the DMUN circuit focusing on precision argumentation, judicial questioning and case-building under pressure. Three beginner-level committees: UN GA Sixth Committee, International Criminal Court and ITLOS.
registration_window: Registrations close shortly before the late-August event

name: DMUN MUNers Forum
description: Online traditional Model UN run by the DMUN Foundation as a training ground for new and experienced delegates. Two-day forum across eight committees under standard parliamentary procedure on current UN agendas. Over 800 delegates expected.
registration_window: Registrations close shortly before the August event

name: DMUN PITCH
description: Online conference on the DMUN circuit with innovation and policy-oriented committees — Startup Parliament, Student Court, Policy Lab Council, SDG Solutions Council, Mental Health Council and Social Media Parliament among them.
registration_window: Registrations close shortly before the mid-October event

name: DMUNLN (DMUN Model League of Nations)
description: Online Model UN simulating the interwar League of Nations, run by the DMUN Foundation. Delegates debate across nine committees covering peacekeeping, refugees, disarmament, economics, labour, intellectual cooperation and colonial mandates. Around 1,800 delegates expected.
registration_window: Registrations close shortly before the April event

name: DMUNP: DMUN Model Parliament and Congress
description: Online Model Parliament and Congress simulation run by the DMUN Foundation. A two-day legislative simulation across three chambers (UK House of Commons, US Congress, India's Lok Sabha) where delegates debate, negotiate and draft legislation on live policy issues.
registration_window: Registrations close shortly before the June event

name: Dorothea Mackellar Poetry Awards
description: Annual Australian poetry writing competition open to students from Kindergarten to Year 12 enrolled in Australian education settings, with an awards ceremony later in the year.
registration_window: Entries usually open March, close late June

name: Drama Scene
description: Weekly term drama classes for young performers.
registration_window: Wednesdays during term

name: Dymocks Beyond Words Creative Writing Competition
description: A creative writing competition run by Dymocks Tutoring.
registration_window: TBA

name: Ethical Explorations Day
description: Ethics and philosophy event for secondary students, exploring moral reasoning and ethical questions through discussion and structured activities. Hosted at Rosebank College.
registration_window: Register through the host school before the event

name: Eureka
description: Primary enrichment competition spanning English, science, mathematics and humanities, with Lower Primary (Years 1–3) and Upper Primary (Years 4–6) divisions.
registration_window: Register before the competition window

name: Exploratory Latin Exam (ELE)
cost: USD 25 per school + USD 7–9 per student
description: Introductory Latin examination for Years 3–8, run by Excellence Through Classics (a committee of the American Classical League). Two levels with an annual theme, offered on paper or online via Lingco.
registration_window: Usually 1 November – 10 February

name: Extracurricular Activity Excellence (EAE Awards)
description: Umbrella entry for the full family of EAE award categories (27 in total), recognising extracurricular achievement. Open for nominations year round.
registration_window: Open for nominations year round. Quarterly review cycles, alternating individual and team entries. Current submission window closes 15 November 2026.

name: FAW Tasmania Beatrice Clarke Award for Young Poets
description: A poetry award for poets aged 14 and under, submitting a poem of up to 40 lines on any theme.
registration_window: Closes 31 August

name: FIRST Robotics Competition (FRC)
cost: Season registration per team (see FIRST Australia)
description: Large-scale high school robotics competition in which teams build industrial-sized robots each season, competing in alliance-based matches at events with awards and judging. Supported in Australia by FIRST Australia.
registration_window: Register before the build season

name: FIRST Tech Challenge (FTC)
cost: Season registration per team (see FIRST Australia)
description: Team-based robotics program in which students design, build and program robots to compete in alliance-based games — a mid-scale step between FIRST LEGO League and FRC. Supported in Australia by FIRST Australia.
registration_window: Register before the season begins

name: Free-Thinkers Forum
description: Philosophy and critical-thinking forum hosted at Rosebank College. Each school sends up to 10 students (1 speaker, 1 adjudicator, remainder as judges and discussion participants). Speeches are judged on originality, engagement and cogency rather than oration. Community of inquiry discussions follow each group of three speeches. Day concludes with a whole-group ethical dilemma. Limited to 9 schools.
registration_window: Book by end of Term 2. Student names, speech topic, teacher details and dietary requirements due Week 3, Term 3.

name: Furious Fiction
description: A monthly flash fiction challenge with a short writing window and a cash prize.
registration_window: First weekend of every month

name: Future Changemakers Program (Harvard Student Agencies)
organiser: Harvard Student Agencies (delivered with Learn With Leaders)
description: A selective online program bringing together high school students from around the world to collaborate with experienced student mentors from top universities. Handpicked fellows identify, brainstorm and solve significant global challenges together.
registration_window: Cohorts run periodically; apply via the website

name: Future Problem Solving Program International (FPSPI)
organiser: Future Problem Solving Program International (Australian affiliate)
description: International problem-solving program in which students research future-focused topics and apply a structured process. Strands include Global Issues, Community Projects and Scenario/Creative Writing, with an Australian affiliate and an international conference pathway.
registration_window: Problem cycles run through the school year

name: Future PsychScholars Competition
description: Formal psychology competition on the Future PsychScholars platform, where high school and undergraduate students showcase psychological research and compete in a structured academic context, including submitting research papers.
registration_window: See website for competition rounds

name: Future PsychScholars OpenChallenge
description: International psychology open challenge hosted on the Future PsychScholars platform — an accessible entry point offering structured challenges that build knowledge, research skills and competitive experience.
registration_window: Rolling challenges; see website for rounds

name: Future Snack Design
description: Open design challenge for an innovative snack concept aimed at a young consumer audience, hosted by Desall with a leading food and beverage company. Open globally.
registration_window: Entries usually due mid-September

name: G.A.T.E.W.A.Y.S
location: Host primary schools across Australia (state based venues; held in Term 4)
cost: Team registration set by GATEWAYS (school based)
description: National team competition for high-ability primary students run by GATEWAYS Education (operating since 1994). Teams rotate through four scenario-based rounds with different academic focuses, structured so no single student can complete a round alone.
registration_window: Schools register ahead of Term 4 event days

name: Global Citizens SDGs Challenge
description: Team challenge in which students brainstorm and create solutions addressing the UN Sustainable Development Goals, supported by workshops, global mentors and cross-cultural exchange.
registration_window: Register before the challenge period opens

name: Global Impact Competition
description: Competition in which students worldwide investigate a community issue through field research and policy writing. Hosted by Build Learning, with cash prizes and a potential internship.
registration_window: Entries usually due mid-June

name: Global Issues Problem Solving Competition
description: Team competition within the Future Problem Solving program: teams of four apply a six-step creative problem-solving process to a global issue scenario. Junior (Years 4–6), Middle (Years 7–9) and Senior (Years 10–12) divisions.
registration_window: Register before the mid-year problem cycle

name: Global Quantum Mechanics Challenge
description: International challenge for high school and university students interested in quantum physics, in a research-oriented but accessible format. Hosted by Edu.Harbour, with cash prizes in the senior category.
registration_window: Entries usually due mid-June

name: Golden Pin Concept Design Award
description: Global call for innovative, not-yet-realised design concepts, hosted by the Taiwan Design Research Institute. Open to students, designers and companies worldwide.
registration_window: Entries usually due mid-June

name: GRC High School Case Competition
cost: Free for GRC High School Branch members; participation fee for non-members
description: Business case competition for high school students run by the Global Research and Consulting Group. Teams solve real-world business problems, supported by skill-building workshops, with top teams recognised and the winners offered a GRC internship.
registration_window: Usually late March – late April

name: Halogen National Young Leaders Day (NYLD)
location: In person (major venues in capital cities)
cost: Per-student ticket (see Halogen for current pricing)
description: Australia's largest gathering of young leaders, run annually by Halogen Australia for primary and secondary students. Students hear high-profile leaders, athletes and identities share insights from their leadership journeys. A leadership event rather than a judged competition.
registration_window: Book before the capital-city event dates

name: Harvard International Review Academic Writing Contest
location: Online (international). Finalists invited to virtual Defense Day.
description: International academic writing contest run by the Harvard International Review for students in grades 7–12. Articles of 800–1,200 words on international affairs; finalists defend their work orally to Harvard IR judges. AI use strictly prohibited.
registration_window: Three submission cycles per year

name: Harvard Model United Nations Australia (HMUN Australia)
description: Four-day international relations simulation bringing Harvard's flagship Model UN conference to the Oceania region. Delegates assume the roles of world leaders, debating global issues and drafting solutions. Run by Harvard College undergraduates in partnership with Crimson Education.
registration_window: Apply before the May conference

name: Hatchlings Fiction Prize
description: A fiction prize for the first 5000 words of a novel plus a pitch, run through the CYA Conference.
registration_window: TBA

name: Hatchlings Picture Book Prize
description: A picture book prize run as part of the CYA Conference.
registration_window: TBA

name: Have Sum Fun Online

description: Monthly online psychology assessment (Psychology Academic Readiness Assessment) from Future PsychScholars: two modules covering psychological fundamentals and research comprehension, webcam-proctored, with official transcripts for university applications.
registration_window: Monthly sittings; retakes permitted

name: Plain English Speaking Award

description: Public speaking competition run by The Arts Unit for NSW students aged 15–18, running since 1978. Up to two contestants per school deliver a prepared and an impromptu speech; the state champion represents NSW at the national final.

name: Poem Forest
description: A nature poetry prize of up to 20 lines on an annual theme, with prizes including book packs, plants and garden tours across primary, secondary, First Nations, language and teacher categories.

name: Point Break Drama
description: Teen acting and screen acting classes covering improvisation, voice, movement, script analysis and camera technique, with four performances each year.

name: Premier's Debating Challenge — Years 11 & 12

description: NSW-wide debating competition run by The Arts Unit for Years 11–12, open to government and non-government schools. All debates are one-hour preparation debates; zone and regional rounds lead to a state final at the University of Sydney Great Hall.

name: Premier's Debating Challenge — Years 7 & 8
location: Zone, regional and state rounds across NSW. State final at The Arts Unit, Lewisham.
organiser: The Arts Unit (NSW Department of Education)
cost: Fee applies for non-government schools (contact Arts Unit)
description: NSW-wide debating competition run by The Arts Unit for Years 7–8, open to government and non-government schools. All debates are one-hour preparation debates, with zone winners progressing through regional rounds to the state final.
registration_window: Rounds run through the year by zone

name: Premier's Debating Challenge — Years 9 & 10
location: Zone, regional and state rounds across NSW
organiser: The Arts Unit (NSW Department of Education)
cost: Fee applies for non-government schools (contact Arts Unit)
description: NSW-wide debating competition run by The Arts Unit for Years 9–10, open to government and non-government schools. All debates are one-hour preparation debates, progressing through zone, regional and state rounds.
registration_window: Rounds run through the year by zone

name: Prime Minister's Spelling Bee
description: Free national online spelling competition for Australian students in Years 3–8, with a dedicated Years 3–4 level. School-based online rounds lead to state and national finals.
registration_window: School round usually runs late July to August

name: Purple Comet! Math Meet
location: Online (sat at school under adult supervision)
description: Free annual international online team mathematics competition for middle and high school students, run since 2003 and sponsored by AwesomeMath. Teams of up to six are given 90 minutes to solve 30 problems within a flexible ten-day window.
registration_window: Register before the ten-day April contest window

name: Python.Comp
description: Coding competition for school students to demonstrate Python programming skills, run by Grok Academy.
registration_window: Register via Grok Academy before the event

name: Radical Innovation Hospitality Product
description: Open innovation challenge for a hospitality product improving the hotel guest experience, hosted by Radical Innovation. Open globally including Oceania.
registration_window: Entries usually due early August

name: Radicepura Garden Festival — Call for Ideas
description: International call for garden design ideas for the Radicepura Garden Festival in Sicily, on an annual theme. Winning projects are physically realised at the Radicepura Horticultural Park.
registration_window: Entries usually due late October

name: Readers Cup
location: In person (regional competitions and state finals)
description: Statewide reading competition run by the Children's Book Council of Australia. Teams of 4–5 read a set book list together then compete in quiz rounds, with regional winners progressing to a State Final. Year 5/6, 7/8 and 9/10 divisions.
registration_window: Register before regional rounds; books announced in advance

name: Reflections in Blue Art Competition
description: Online art exhibition and competition for artists worldwide interpreting the theme 'Reflections in Blue'. Hosted by Megalopolitan Art Gallery.
registration_window: Entries usually due late May

name: Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF)
description: The world's premier pre-university science and engineering fair. Students qualify through affiliated local, regional or national fairs, then compete internationally under Society for Science rules for substantial prizes and scholarships.
registration_window: Qualify through affiliated local/regional/national fairs

name: RoboCup Junior
location: Australia (state based events plus national championships)
description: Project-based robotics competition pathway with leagues including Rescue Line, Rescue Maze, OnStage and Soccer, across regional, state and national events, with qualification to international RoboCupJunior.
registration_window: Register per event; regional events lead to nationals

name: Rostrum Voice of Youth
location: School-based first round; state final and national final at Independent Theatre, North Sydney
description: National public speaking competition run by Rostrum Australia. Junior (Years 7–9) and Senior (Years 10–12) divisions; contestants deliver a six-minute prepared original speech, progressing from school entry to state and national finals.
registration_window: First round March; finals mid-year

name: RYLA (Rotary Youth Leadership Awards)
location: Rotating NSW host school (e.g. Knox Grammar, Wahroonga)
cost: Free (fully funded by local Rotary clubs)
description: Intensive week-long residential leadership program run by Rotary District 9685 for young people with leadership potential.
registration_window: Nominations earlier in the year; held in January

name: RYPEN (Rotary Youth Program of Enrichment)
location: Various NSW camp venues (Blue Mountains region falls under District 9685)
cost: Varies by Rotary district (some camps free)
description: Weekend residential enrichment camp run by Rotary for students aged roughly 14–16, building confidence, public speaking, teamwork and life skills.
registration_window: Nominations via local Rotary clubs

name: Samsung Solve for Tomorrow
description: National STEM competition run by Samsung in which students ideate solutions to real-world community problems, with major prize packages for winning schools. Emphasises innovation, critical thinking, collaboration and community responsibility.
registration_window: Entries usually due mid-year

name: SBMUN (Sydney Boys High School Model United Nations)
location: Sydney Boys High School, 556 Cleveland St, Moore Park NSW 2021
description: Student-run Model UN conference hosted by Sydney Boys High School, welcoming both first-time and experienced delegates from across Sydney for debate, diplomacy and problem solving on global issues.
registration_window: Register via Humanitix ahead of the December conference

name: Science and Engineering Challenge (SEC)
description: Nationwide STEM outreach competition presented by the University of Newcastle with communities and sponsors. Run as Challenge Days for Years 9–10, with pathways to state and national finals.
registration_window: Schools book Challenge Days through the year

name: SCRIBO Latin Writing Contest
cost: USD 20 per school + USD 7.50–8.50 per student
description: Latin composition contest run by Excellence Through Classics (a committee of the American Classical League). Students write in Latin in response to an annual theme. A writing contest rather than a timed multiple-choice exam, composed and submitted online.
registration_window: Usually 1 September – 15 March

name: SEAMO (Southeast Asian Mathematical Olympiad)
location: Online via partner providers (SEAMO X final in Bali)
organiser: SEAMO (via approved providers e.g. EduVision Australia)
cost: ~SGD 12 (about AUD 14) per student; optional SEAMO X package extra
description: International mathematics olympiad (founded 2016) engaging 50,000+ students across 15+ countries, with paper levels for Grades 1–12. The top performers are invited to the SEAMO X international round. All participants receive a personalised performance report.
registration_window: Register via a partner provider before the January contest

name: Slinkies Young Writers Anthology
description: A young writers' anthology and call out run by Short Australian Stories.
registration_window: TBA

name: Spooky Story Competition
description: A short story competition on a spooky theme run by the KSP Writers' Centre.
registration_window: Entries close mid March

name: Stanford Symbolic Systems Society High School Essay Competition
description: International high school essay competition run by the Stanford Symbolic Systems Society, drawing on the intersection of computer science, psychology, cognition, mathematics, philosophy and linguistics. Winning essays are published in the society's journal, Machina.
registration_window: Entries usually due late January

name: STEM Racing
cost: Regional free; state/national finals charged per team
description: The foremost student STEM competition, in which teams design and build miniature racing vehicles. More than 17,000 schools across 51 nations take part. Regional competitions lead to state and national finals.
registration_window: Register before the regional competition season

name: Storyathon
description: Free online story-writing event in which primary students write 100-word microstories on a set theme, published in a class ebook. Runs multiple times a year.
registration_window: Runs several times a year; register before each event window

name: Storyfest National Novella Writing Competition
description: A novella competition for secondary students under 19, with entries between 8000 and 20000 words.
registration_window: Closes 5 December

name: Storyfest National Poetry Prize
description: A poetry prize for secondary students with junior and senior categories, accepting poems up to 50 lines on any subject.
registration_window: TBA

name: SUBS in Schools
description: Technology challenge in which teams design, build and test model submarines or ROV-style systems, exploring maritime engineering, hydrodynamics, electronics and coding. Managed in Australia by the REA Foundation.
registration_window: Register before the competition season

name: Sydney Philosothon
description: Inter-school philosophy competition run annually since 2009. Teams of four (two junior, two senior) take part in three facilitated Communities of Inquiry, assessed by trained teachers and philosophers, with stimulus material provided in advance.
registration_window: Register ahead of the late-July evening event

name: The Ethics Centre Young Writers' Competition
description: An essay competition of up to 800 words responding to set ethical questions, with categories for ages 13 to 17 and 18 to 29.
registration_window: Closes 8 September

name: The Junior Academy (NYAS)
organiser: The New York Academy of Sciences
description: Online program run by the New York Academy of Sciences connecting students aged 13–17 in a global community to collaborate on virtual innovation challenges with STEM mentors.
registration_window: Applications open per intake (see NYAS)

name: The Simpson Prize
organiser: Simpson Prize and the Australian Government
description: A national history competition for Years 9 and 10 responding to an Anzac and First World War themed question.
registration_window: Usually closes November

name: The UN Voice Competition
description: Public speaking competition on global and UN-themed issues for Years 7–10, developing oratory, research and persuasive argument.
registration_window: Register before the competition rounds

name: The Western Civilisation Program Summer School (ACU)
cost: See ACU (scholarship places have been offered)
description: Summer school run by ACU's Western Civilisation Program, giving senior students a taste of great-books style study — philosophy, literature, art and history of the Western tradition. Confirm current intake details with ACU.
registration_window: Applications ahead of the summer school period

name: The Worlds Scholars Cup
location: Regional host schools (then Global Round and finals)
description: International team academic competition (teams of three) spanning debate, collaborative writing, a quiz (Scholar's Challenge) and the Scholar's Bowl, across a multi-subject curriculum. Regional rounds lead to a Global Round and the Tournament of Champions.
registration_window: Register before the regional round

name: Think Essay Prize (Royal Institute of Philosophy)
description: International philosophy essay competition for students aged 15–18, run by the Royal Institute of Philosophy. Six prompts each year (often including a philosophy-of-mind question). The winning essay is published in the journal Think.
registration_window: Entries usually due around 20 April

name: Toastmasters Youth Leadership Program
location: Global; run locally in Australia through Toastmasters clubs
cost: Low cost; depends on the sponsoring club (kit fee)
description: A workshop of eight one to two hour sessions for those aged 14 to 18, developing communication and leadership skills through practical experience. Presented during or after school or on weekends, coordinated by a sponsoring Toastmasters club or cooperating school. Related Gavel Clubs cater for younger students.
registration_window: Runs when a local club organises a program; contact a nearby Toastmasters club

name: Toga Day (School Event)
description: Internal school classics event for Years 7–10. Students make their own togas and take part in classics-themed activities celebrating Roman life and culture — a hands-on, whole-cohort event rather than an external competition.
registration_window: Internal — organised by the classics faculty

name: Tournament of Minds TOM
location: At school plus regional competition day
cost: Approx. AUD 300 per school + AUD 50 per team
description: Team problem-solving program in which teams of 5–7 students work on a long-term challenge over six weeks, then present their solution plus tackle a spontaneous challenge. Regional rounds lead to state and international finals.
registration_window: Register before Term 3 regional rounds

name: Tournament of Towns
location: International. Australian sittings hosted in Sydney, Melbourne, Adelaide, Brisbane, Perth and Canberra. Some online options.
organiser: Tournament of Towns (via Australian city hosts)
description: Long-running international mathematical olympiad (founded 1980) prizing deep, proof-based problem solving — five hours per paper, with O-level (easier) and A-level (harder) papers in each of two annual rounds. Australian sittings hosted in major cities.
registration_window: Two rounds per year (spring and autumn sittings)

name: UN Youth Evatt Model UN
cost: Set by state division (see registration page)
description: UN Security Council simulation run by UN Youth, in which pairs of delegates represent member states across preliminary debates, with semi-finals, finals and National Finals for top teams.
registration_window: Preliminary rounds run May to July

name: UN Youth Junior Leadership Summit (JLS)
description: NSW-exclusive two-day introductory summit for Years 7–8 run by UN Youth, focused on leadership, problem solving, communication and advocacy through interactive workshops — a skills-first alternative to Model UN debates.
registration_window: Register ahead of the summit dates

name: UN Youth Negotiations Competition
location: Online (preliminary rounds), Sydney (semi finals and grand finals)
description: Public speaking and diplomacy competition simulating international negotiations. Pairs represent a country's stance on an international issue and negotiate with an opposing pair toward a mutually beneficial outcome. Online preliminaries; finals in Sydney.
registration_window: Rounds run late July to mid-August

name: UN Youth NSW State Conference
cost: Around AUD 270–310 per student (includes accommodation, food and activities)
description: Overnight residential conference run by UN Youth NSW for Years 9–12, combining workshops, speaker panels, case studies, Interactive Problem Solving and Model UN debates around an annual theme.
registration_window: Early-bird and regular windows close before the March conference

name: UN Youth Summits (NSW)
description: One-day UN Youth events exploring complex topics in international affairs, law and global politics through workshops and Interactive Problem Solving simulations. Three themed summits run through the year.
registration_window: Three summits per year; register before each

name: UN Youth Voice Public Speaking
cost: Set by state division (see registration page)
description: Public speaking competition run by UN Youth focusing on civics and problem solving. Students pitch a solution to a global or local issue and answer questions, progressing through regional, state and national rounds.
registration_window: State calendars vary; rounds run through the year

name: UN Youth Workshops
cost: Usually free or low cost (arranged with schools)
description: In-school workshops run by UN Youth volunteers on global issues, public speaking and Model UN skills, arranged directly with schools throughout the year.
registration_window: Arranged with schools through the year

name: Unbox Architecture Competition
description: International architecture ideas competition from Volume Zero challenging entrants to rethink the DNA of our shared environments. Open globally with a USD 10,000 prize pool.
registration_window: Entries usually due early December

name: University of Melbourne Schools Maths Olympics (SMO)
location: University of Melbourne Parkville campus, Victoria
organiser: Melbourne University Mathematics and Statistics Society (MUMS)

description: Fast-paced, teamwork-centred maths competition run by the Melbourne University Mathematics and Statistics Society at the Parkville campus. Teams race through timed head-to-head problem rounds; winners are invited to the University Maths Olympics against university students.

name: UNSW Bragg Student Prize for Science Writing
description: A science writing prize for students in Years 7 to 10, submitting a short essay on an annual theme.
registration_window: TBA

name: UNSW DiscoverMUN and MUNiS
location: UNSW Sydney (DiscoverMUN) / visiting schools across Sydney and NSW (MUNiS)
description: Two outreach programs from the UNSW UN Society: DiscoverMUN, an annual one-day on-campus MUN event for high schoolers, and MUNiS, where UNSW students visit schools to teach the UN and run MUN simulations. All skill levels welcome.
registration_window: DiscoverMUN annual; MUNiS ongoing by arrangement

name: UNSW School Mathematics Competition
location: Sat at school across NSW and ACT; prize-giving at UNSW Sydney
organiser: UNSW School of Mathematics and Statistics
description: Annual mathematics competition run since 1962 by the UNSW School of Mathematics and Statistics. A three-hour open-book exam designed to assess mathematical insight and ingenuity rather than routine technique. Junior (up to Year 10) and Senior (Years 11–12) divisions, for NSW and ACT students.
registration_window: Entries usually close early May; sat in June

name: UoN High Performing Students Program
description: University of Newcastle program for high-performing senior students, offering university-level study and enrichment while at school. Confirm current structure and intake details with UoN.
registration_window: Applications via school nomination (see UoN)

name: Voiceworks
description: A literary magazine publishing fiction, nonfiction, poetry and art from writers under 25, with editorial feedback.
registration_window: Year round submissions

name: Web.Comp
description: Web design competition for school students to showcase web development and design skills, run by Grok Academy.
registration_window: Register via Grok Academy before the event

name: What Matters? Writing Competition (Whitlam Institute)
description: National writing competition run by the Whitlam Institute inviting students in Years 5–12 to share what matters to them in 600 words or less. Entries may be fiction, non-fiction, persuasive writing, poetry or prose. Both a creative writing exercise and a civics activity.
registration_window: Entries usually open early in the year

name: World Council for Gifted and Talented Children (WCGTC)
organiser: World Council for Gifted and Talented Children
description: International advocacy and research organisation for gifted education, connecting educators, researchers and parents worldwide. Runs the biennial World Conference and publishes research — a professional reference resource rather than a student competition.

name: World Economics Cup

name: World Economics Cup Global Final
description: Culminating world final round of the World Economics Cup for qualifying teams.
registration_window: Qualification required. Registration closes 1 October 2026.

name: World Robot Olympiad (WRO)
description: Global robotics competition with categories including RoboMission, RoboSports, Future Innovators and Future Engineers, for ages roughly 8–19. Entered via national organisers, with winners progressing to the international final.
registration_window: Register via the national organiser before regional rounds

name: Write a Book in a Day
organiser: Write a Book in a Day (The Kids' Cancer Project)
cost: AUD 77 per team + minimum AUD 240 sponsorship
description: Teams of 5–10 write and illustrate a complete book within a 12-hour period, including five random words. Books are donated to children in hospital and fundraising supports childhood cancer research.
registration_window: Choose any 12-hour day between June and September

name: Write the World
description: Monthly genre based writing competitions for writers aged 13 to 19, with peer and expert review and cash prizes.
registration_window: Monthly competitions

name: WriteOn

registration_window: Register before the virtual hackathon begins

name: Yale Foreign Policy Initiative High School Essay Contest
description: International essay competition for high school students run by the Yale Foreign Policy Initiative, focused on foreign policy, international security and global governance. Winning essays may be featured in Yale FPI publications.
registration_window: Entries usually due around April

name: Yale Review of International Studies (YRIS) High School Essay Contest
description: International essay contest run by the Yale Review of International Studies exclusively for high school students. Essays under 1,500 words on an annual international-relations prompt.
registration_window: Entries usually due end of June

name: Yale YIRA Global Essay Competition
description: International essay competition for students in grades 8–12 run by the Yale International Relations Association, on topics spanning international relations, global affairs and diplomacy. Top 50 finalists announced (10 per grade).
registration_window: Entries usually due mid-to-late December

name: YLAA Secondary Youth Leadership Conference

description: A one day leadership conference for secondary students run by a youth led not for profit, featuring keynote speakers and interactive facilitators. Tailored in school leadership programs are also available for whole year levels or student leadership teams.
registration_window: Conferences run in Term 1 (February to March); schools book in advance via the website

name: Young ICT Explorers YICTE
description: Project-based technology competition in which students (individuals or teams of up to four) create an ICT project of their choice and present it with a written report. Around $30,000 in cash prizes awarded annually, including a Best Use of AI category.
registration_window: Submissions due ahead of Term 3–4 regional showcases

name: Young Justice Program (Law Society of NSW)
location: Rotates annually across NSW (2024: Campbelltown, WSU; 2025: Wollongong)
description: Annual one-day program run by the Law Society of NSW where students explore law and justice with leading legal professionals, including the Chief Justice of NSW. Rotates between metropolitan and regional NSW locations each year.
registration_window: Schools nominate students ahead of the August event

name: Young Minds Prize (Minds Underground)
description: International essay competition for students aged 14 and under, run by Minds Underground. Two age categories (8–11 and 12–14) engaging with thought-provoking questions across science, humanities and creative expression.
